active_mainline: 1D normal layer-LJ in continuous physical time t, using the full nonlinear LJ force without global Taylor or harmonic closure
state: P(lambda,t) is constrained by an exact instantaneous shape law derived from the first two spacing-velocity moment equations; the required fields are conditional velocity variance Theta, mean-flow material acceleration D_t u, and conditional nonlinear-LJ acceleration from neighboring-spacing joint states
current_result: Where a smooth continuum representation has P>0 and conditional velocity variance Theta>0, the exact first two phase-space moment equations imply d_lambda log P = (a_bar - D_t u)/Theta - d_lambda log Theta. Hence P(lambda,t) = C(t)/Theta(lambda,t) times exp[integral (a_bar-D_t u)/Theta d lambda]. The original nonlinear layer-LJ law enters exactly through a_bar = m_plus + m_minus - 2 phi'(lambda), where m_plus/minus are conditional neighboring-spacing force means obtained from ordered P2 states. This is an instantaneous function-form constraint, not a named distribution closure. The older exponential-LJ family is recovered only under the restrictive special conditions of lambda-independent Theta, zero D_t u, and central-spacing-independent neighbor-force means.
next_target: Record spacing and spacing velocity simultaneously in the deterministic chain, estimate u(lambda,t), Theta(lambda,t), D_t u(lambda,t), and a_bar(lambda,t), and test the exact measured log-slope identity under bin/grid refinement before introducing any closure for neighboring-spacing P2.
